procedures.title: Starting the Engine (B25/C35 Instrument Panel)
preconditions: Put remote control handle in NEUTRAL
steps: Turn on power switch on instrument panel
Push start switch and hold for maximum 15 seconds
Release start switch after engine starts
Check gauges indicators and alarms are normal
Check for water fuel or oil leakage
Check smoke color engine vibration and sound are normal
Check seawater discharge from outlet
procedures.expected_outcome: Engine starts successfully and runs normally with proper seawater discharge
warnings: Never jump-start the engine
Never hold starter for longer than 15 seconds or starter motor will overheat
Ensure boat is clear of obstacles when testing gear engagement

procedures.title: Starting the Engine (VC10 Vessel Control System)
preconditions: Press Power switch on selected station
Enter password if Sys on by ID is set
steps: Press control head SEL switch
Wait for display to show engine data
Move remote control handle to N Neutral position
Press Engine START/STOP switch
Check engine conditions on VC10 display
Verify all systems are operating normally
procedures.expected_outcome: Engine starts and VC10 display shows normal engine conditions
warnings: Engine will not start if Power switch is OFF
Do not press START/STOP switch except for stopping engine

procedures.title: Starting the Engine (VC20 Vessel Control System)
preconditions: Press Power switch on selected station
Enter password if Sys on by ID is set
steps: Press control head SEL switch
Wait for display to show engine data
Enter password if Start by ID is set
Move remote control handle to N Neutral position
Press Engine START/STOP switch
Check engine conditions on VC20 display
procedures.expected_outcome: Engine starts and VC20 display shows normal engine conditions
warnings: Hold key fob in front of blinking lamp for authentication
Engine will not start if Power switch is OFF

procedures.title: Normal Engine Shutdown (B25/C35 Instrument Panel)
preconditions: Remote control handle in forward or reverse position
steps: Reduce engine speed to low idle
Put remote control handle in NEUTRAL
Race engine 5 times by accelerating from low to high speed
Allow engine to run at low speed without load for 5 minutes
Push and hold stop switch until engine completely stops
Push power switch off
Wait 6 seconds before turning battery switch off
Close fuel cock
Close seacock if equipped
procedures.expected_outcome: Engine shuts down properly and safely
warnings: Continue to hold stop switch until engine completely stops
Do not turn battery switch off immediately after power switch

procedures.title: Normal Engine Shutdown (VC10/VC20/VC30 Systems)
steps: Move remote control handle to N Neutral position
Cool engine down at low speed below 1000 min-1 for about 5 minutes
Press Engine START/STOP switch on selected station
Press Power switch and turn power OFF
Wait 6 seconds or more before turning battery switch off
Turn battery switch off
Close fuel tank cock
Close seacock
procedures.expected_outcome: Engine shuts down properly through vessel control system
warnings: Do not press START/STOP switch when engine is stopped or it will restart
Allow 5 minutes cooling for turbocharger equipped engines

procedures.title: Bleeding the Fuel System
steps: Check fuel level in fuel tank and refill if necessary
Open fuel cock of fuel tank
Loosen air bleed screw two to three turns
Push up and down on priming pump to release air approximately 60 times
Continue pumping until stream of fuel with no air bubbles flows
Tighten air bleed screw
procedures.expected_outcome: Fuel system is properly primed with no air bubbles in fuel lines
warnings: Diesel fuel is flammable and explosive
Always wear safety glasses when bleeding fuel system

procedures.title: Checking Engine Oil Level
preconditions: Engine has been stopped for sufficient time for oil to settle
steps: Make sure engine is level
Remove dipstick and wipe with clean cloth
Fully reinsert dipstick
Remove dipstick and check oil level
Oil level should be between upper and lower lines on dipstick
Add oil if necessary
Fully reinsert dipstick
procedures.expected_outcome: Oil level is confirmed to be between minimum and maximum marks on dipstick
warnings: Prevent dirt and debris from contaminating engine oil
Never overfill engine with oil

procedures.title: Changing Engine Oil and Filter (Initial 50 Hours)
preconditions: Engine oil is warm for easier draining
steps: Turn engine off
Remove engine oil dipstick
Attach oil drain pump if equipped and pump out oil
Remove engine oil filter with filter wrench turning counterclockwise
Install new filter element hand tight until seal touches housing
Turn filter additional 3/4 turn clockwise
Fill with new engine oil to proper level
Perform trial run and check for oil leaks
Check oil level 10 minutes after stopping engine
procedures.expected_outcome: Fresh oil and filter installed with no leaks and proper oil level
warnings: Hot oil can cause burns
Never mix different types of engine oil
Never overfill with oil

procedures.title: Changing Engine Oil and Filter (Every 250 Hours)
preconditions: Engine oil is warm for easier draining
steps: Turn engine off
Remove engine oil dipstick
Attach oil drain pump if equipped and pump out oil
Remove engine oil filter with filter wrench turning counterclockwise
Install new filter element hand tight until seal touches housing
Turn filter additional 3/4 turn clockwise
Fill with new engine oil to proper level
Perform trial run and check for oil leaks
Check oil level 10 minutes after stopping engine
procedures.expected_outcome: Fresh oil and filter installed with no leaks and proper oil level
warnings: Hot oil can cause burns
Never mix different types of engine oil
Never overfill with oil

procedures.title: Draining Fuel Filter/Water Separator (Every 50 Hours)
preconditions: Approved container available to catch fuel
Fuel tank cock can be accessed
steps: Close fuel tank cock
Loosen clamp screw and remove fire-resistant cover
Attach tube to drain plug
Loosen drain plug at bottom by turning counterclockwise
Drain off any water or sediment until clean fuel flows
Tighten drain plug
Remove drain tube
Install fire-resistant cover and tighten clamp screw
Bleed air from fuel system
procedures.expected_outcome: Water and contaminants removed from fuel system
warnings: Fuel system is under pressure
Never use shop rag to catch fuel
Wipe up spills immediately

procedures.title: Replacing Fuel Filter Element (Every 250 Hours)
steps: Close fuel tank cock
Remove fuel filter with filter wrench
Apply thin film of clean diesel fuel to sealing surface of new filter gasket
Install new filter and hand-tighten
Use filter wrench and tighten to 20-24 N·m
Bleed fuel system
Check for fuel leaks
Dispose of waste properly
procedures.expected_outcome: New fuel filter installed with no leaks and proper fuel flow
warnings: Fuel system is under pressure
Never use shop rag to catch fuel
Wipe up spills immediately

procedures.title: Checking Seawater Pump Impeller
steps: Loosen side cover bolts and remove side cover
Inspect inside of seawater pump with flashlight
Check for cracked or nicked impeller blades
Check for damaged wear plate
If no damage found install O-ring and side cover
If damage found disassemble and replace impeller
Check for water leaks from drain line during operation
procedures.expected_outcome: Seawater pump impeller confirmed in good condition or replaced if damaged
warnings: Large amount of continuous water leak indicates mechanical seal replacement needed

procedures.title: Replacing Seawater Pump Impeller (Every 1000 Hours)
steps: Remove side cover of seawater pump
Install puller in impeller with M18x1.5 thread side toward cover
Turn jack screw clockwise to remove impeller from pump body
Install new impeller ensuring proper orientation
Reassemble pump cover with new O-ring
Test for proper seawater flow
procedures.expected_outcome: New impeller installed and seawater pump functioning properly
warnings: Impeller must be replaced every 1000 hours even if not damaged
Use proper puller tools to avoid damage

procedures.title: Checking and Adding Engine Coolant
steps: Ensure all drain cocks are closed
Loosen coolant filler cap to relieve pressure then remove cap
Pour coolant slowly into coolant tank to avoid air bubbles
Fill until coolant overflows from filler port
Align filler cap tabs with filler port notches
Tighten filler cap firmly
Check coolant level in reservoir should be at FULL mark
Add coolant to reservoir if necessary
Check rubber hose connecting reservoir to heat exchanger
procedures.expected_outcome: Coolant system properly filled and reservoir at correct level
warnings: Never remove filler cap if engine is hot
Never pour cold coolant into hot engine
Always tighten cap securely

procedures.title: Changing Engine Coolant (Every 250 Hours)
preconditions: Approved disposal method for old coolant
steps: Open all coolant drain cocks
Allow to drain completely
Dispose of waste coolant properly
Close all drain cocks
Fill coolant tank and reservoir with appropriate coolant mixture
Check for leaks after refilling
Test engine at operating temperature
Verify proper coolant circulation
procedures.expected_outcome: Fresh coolant installed with proper circulation and no leaks
warnings: Wear eye protection and rubber gloves when handling coolant
Never mix different types of coolant

procedures.title: Checking and Adjusting Alternator V-ribbed Belt Tension
preconditions: Engine has run at idle for 5 minutes then stopped
steps: Remove belt cover
Check belt by pushing middle with finger using 100 N force
Belt should deflect 8 to 9 mm with proper tension
Loosen 3 alternator bolts
Screw in adjusting bolt and move alternator to adjust tension
Tighten 3 alternator bolts
Install belt cover
Inspect belt for wear frayed cords or damage
procedures.expected_outcome: Belt tension properly adjusted and belt condition verified
warnings: Perform check with power and battery switches off
Never get oil on belt as it causes slipping
Check belt fits properly in ribbed grooves

procedures.title: Checking Battery Electrolyte Level (Serviceable Batteries)
preconditions: Eye protection and protective clothing available
steps: Turn off battery switch or disconnect negative battery cable
Remove battery plugs and check electrolyte level in all cells
If level is below minimum fill with distilled water to upper limit
Maximum fill level is 10-15 mm above plates
Replace plugs securely
Reconnect battery cable if disconnected
procedures.expected_outcome: Battery electrolyte at proper levels in all cells
warnings: Battery contains sulfuric acid
Always wear safety goggles and protective clothing
Never operate with insufficient electrolyte

procedures.title: Cleaning Intake Silencer Air Cleaner Element
steps: Disassemble intake silencer air cleaner
Remove element from housing
Clean element and housing with neutral detergent
Rinse thoroughly with clean water
Dry completely before reassembly
Reassemble intake silencer ensuring proper sealing
procedures.expected_outcome: Clean air cleaner element properly installed for optimal air flow
warnings: Ensure element is completely dry before installation

procedures.title: Preparing Engine for Long-term Storage
preconditions: Engine will not be used for extended period
Access to engine exterior and systems
steps: Wipe off dust or oil from engine exterior
Drain water from fuel filters
Drain fuel tank completely or fill tank to prevent condensation
Grease exposed areas and joints of remote control cables
Seal intake silencer exhaust pipe to prevent moisture entry
Completely drain bilge in hull bottom
Waterproof engine room to prevent rain or seawater entry
Charge battery once monthly
Make sure power switch is off
procedures.expected_outcome: Engine properly prepared for extended storage without damage
warnings: Do not drain coolant system
If seawater left inside may freeze and damage cooling system

procedures.title: Draining Seawater Cooling System
steps: Open seawater drain cock on marine gear cooler if equipped
Open seawater drain cock on air cooler for 4JH80/4JH110 models
Remove four bolts attaching seawater pump side cover
Remove cover and drain seawater from pump
Install cover and tighten bolts
Close all drain cocks after draining complete
procedures.expected_outcome: All seawater drained from cooling system to prevent freeze damage
warnings: Seawater left inside may freeze and damage cooling system below 0°C

procedures.title: Returning Engine to Service After Storage
preconditions: Engine has been in long-term storage
steps: Replace oil and oil filter before running engine
Supply fuel if fuel tank was drained and prime fuel system
Confirm there is engine coolant in the engine
Operate engine at idle speed for 1 minute
Check fluid levels and inspect engine for leaks
Perform normal operational checks
procedures.expected_outcome: Engine returned to service safely with all systems functioning properly
warnings: Replace oil and filter before running
Check all fluid levels before operation

procedures.title: Daily Engine Inspection Checks
steps: Check for engine oil leaks around engine
Check for fuel leaks especially high-pressure lines
Check for engine coolant leaks
Check for damaged or missing parts
Check for loose missing or damaged fasteners
Check electrical harnesses for damage or corrosion
Check hoses for cracks abrasions and damaged clamps
Check fuel filter water separator for water and contaminants
Check diesel fuel engine oil and coolant levels
procedures.expected_outcome: Engine confirmed in good condition with no leaks or damage before operation
warnings: Never check for fuel leak with hands due to high-pressure spray danger
Take corrective action before operating if problems found

procedures.title: Remote Control Cable Adjustment
preconditions: Remote control handle operates but needs adjustment
steps: For marine gear remote control ensure handle moves to correct NEUTRAL FORWARD REVERSE positions
Use NEUTRAL position as standard for adjustment
Loosen and retighten cable fitting to adjust
For engine speed control ensure control lever moves to high-speed and low-speed stop positions
Loosen adjustment screw for remote control cable
Adjust low-speed stop position first then high-speed stop position
Test operation through full range of motion
procedures.expected_outcome: Remote control handle operates smoothly with proper engagement at all positions
warnings: Improper adjustment can prevent proper gear engagement or engine speed control

procedures.title: Engine Break-in Procedure (First 50 Hours)
preconditions: New engine with less than 50 hours operation
Vessel can operate at various speeds
steps: During first 10 hours do not operate at WOT for more than 1 minute at time
From 10 to 50 hours run engine at maximum speed minus 400 min-1 most of time
Every 30 minutes run 10 minutes at maximum minus 200 min-1
Every 30 minutes run 4-5 minutes at WOT wide open throttle
Do not operate at low speed light load for more than 30 minutes
If operating at low speed race engine by accelerating from low to high speed 5 times
procedures.expected_outcome: Engine properly broken in for optimal performance and longevity
warnings: Do not exceed 1 minute WOT during first 10 hours
Racing engine cleans carbon from cylinders and injection valves

procedures.title: Trolling Operation (KMH4A Marine Gear Only)
preconditions: Engine equipped with KMH4A marine gear
steps: Reduce engine speed to low idle less than 1000 min-1 before engaging trolling
Move trolling handle from high speed H to desired low speed L position
Adjust speed to desired trolling rate
Secure trolling handle in position
Before returning to normal operation put trolling handle in high-speed H position
Increase engine speed and continue normal operation
procedures.expected_outcome: Engine operates at controlled low speed suitable for trolling
warnings: Reduce engine speed before engaging trolling
Return to high-speed position before normal operation

procedures.title: Warm Up Mode Operation (Vessel Control Systems)
steps: Move remote control handle to N Neutral position
NEUTRAL lamp will come on
Press NTRL switch of selected station control head
NEUTRAL lamp will flash
Move remote control handle to control engine speed while gear remains in neutral
To cancel warm up mode move handle to N Neutral and press NTRL switch again
procedures.expected_outcome: Engine speed can be controlled while transmission remains in neutral for warm up
warnings: Only available with vessel control systems VC10 VC20 VC30

procedures.title: Engine Speed Limit Mode (Vessel Control Systems)
preconditions: Engine running in forward idle position
steps: Move remote control handle to Forward Idle position
Press NTRL switch of selected station
Lamp above NTRL switch will flash
Engine speed will be limited to preset value even with full throttle
To release mode move handle to Neutral Forward Idle or Reverse Idle position
Press NTRL switch to release Engine Speed Limit Mode
procedures.expected_outcome: Engine speed limited to safe preset value regardless of throttle position
warnings: Default setting is 50% of maximum engine speed
Only available with vessel control systems

procedures.title: YANMAR E-key Registration (VC20/VC30 Systems)
preconditions: Up to 10 key fobs available for registration
steps: Select YANMAR E-key ON from MAIN MENU
When key registration screen displays switch panel lamp blinks
Hold key fob over blinking key icon on switch panel
Confirm registration status updates on display
Repeat for additional keys up to 10 maximum
Close key registration screen to complete process
procedures.expected_outcome: Key fobs registered and authentication function enabled for system power on
warnings: If you lose key contact authorized dealer
Key reset required for countries without radio certification

procedures.title: Emergency Engine Stop Procedures
preconditions: Emergency situation requiring immediate engine shutdown
steps: Press Emergency Stop switch on switch panel immediately
Engine will stop immediately
Emergency Stop screen will show on display with audible alarm
After emergency passes press Emergency Stop switch to release
For instrument panel systems press Engine Auxiliary Stop switch on ECU cover
Turn switch to RUN position to release
Alternative emergency method turn off battery switch for engine control unit
procedures.expected_outcome: Engine stops immediately for emergency situations
warnings: Use only in emergency situations
Normal shutdown procedures should be used under normal circumstances
Engine cannot restart while emergency stop is active

procedures.title: Backup Panel Operation
preconditions: Remote control handle in NEUTRAL position
steps: Ensure power switch on switch panel is OFF
Ensure remote control handle is in N Neutral position
Press power switch to ON position on backup panel
Lamp will come on indicating backup panel is enabled
Engine can be started or stopped with START/STOP switch
Adjust engine speed using sub throttle control volume
Turn fully anti-clockwise before starting
For shutdown turn sub throttle fully anti-clockwise before stopping
procedures.expected_outcome: Engine can be controlled through backup panel in emergency
warnings: Use only in emergency when primary controls fail
Always move throttle fully anti-clockwise first
Shift switch does not work on common rail engines
